calibration_constraint: All parameters are population-dependent. No universal cultural conditioning parameters. Flag any as error.

mechanism_chain.process: Occupant perceives architectural material identity (wood, stone, concrete, steel, glass, fabric). Material identity is classified via visual and haptic processing.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Ventral visual stream (material categorization); somatosensory cortex (haptic confirmation)

mechanism_chain.process: Material identity activates learned evaluative associations stored in long-term memory. These associations are culturally acquired through repeated exposure to material-context pairings in the occupant's cultural environment (marble in banks = wealth/trust; exposed brick in cafés = authenticity/informality; raw concrete in prisons = austerity/oppression).
mechanism_chain.substrate: Inferior temporal cortex (material categorization) → medial temporal (associative memory) → orbitofrontal (evaluation)

mechanism_chain.process: Evaluative associations modulate the affective response to the material: culturally positive associations amplify innate hedonic response; culturally negative associations suppress or reverse it. This modulation operates on TOP of the biophilic baseline from NATURAL_MATERIAL_CONVERGENCE_001.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Top-down modulation from mPFC/OFC on amygdala and insular cortex

biophilic_baseline.interpretation: Innate biophilic baseline: evolutionary familiarity → positive; evolutionary novelty → negative. This baseline is UNIVERSAL but SMALL relative to cultural modifier.

cultural_modifier_examples.note: These values are for Western European cultural context ONLY. Other populations require independent parameter estimation.

cultural_modifier_nordic.wood: +0.40 (cultural amplification of biophilic baseline; wood = national identity)
cultural_modifier_nordic.raw_concrete: -0.10 (less negative than Western European; Nordic modernism tradition)

cultural_modifier_japanese.wood_hinoki: +0.45 (sacred/pure associations; highest studied cultural wood amplification)
cultural_modifier_japanese.tatami_woven_grass: +0.30 (cultural domestic warmth; unique to Japanese context)

architectural_education.effect: Architecturally educated individuals show different cultural conditioning: concrete may be evaluated positively (appreciation of brutalism), glass positively (modernist transparency). Education partially overrides default cultural associations.

socioeconomic_status.effect: SES modulates material evaluations: marble and glass are evaluated more positively by higher-SES occupants (aspirational associations); wood and brick more positively by middle-SES (comfort/authenticity associations).

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Cultural material associations include interoceptive predictions: wood predicts warmth (body budget credit), concrete predicts cold (body budget debit), regardless of actual surface temperature. These are learned interoceptive predictions that may be culturally specific.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Culturally familiar materials enhance perceived control through predictability — the occupant knows what to expect from the material (how it feels, what it connotes). Culturally unfamiliar materials reduce perceived control by introducing material uncertainty.

cross_template_references: NATURAL_MATERIAL_CONVERGENCE_001 — biophilic baseline is the innate layer; cultural conditioning is the learned layer
MSI_CONGRUENCY_PRINCIPLE_001 — cultural expectations create crossmodal predictions (visual wood → expected warm haptic → congruency if confirmed)
MATERIAL_AGING_TEMPORAL_DEPTH_001 — cultural attitudes toward aging/patina modulate temporal depth evaluation
name: Material-Cultural Conditioning and Evaluative Association

cultural_alignment_score.interpretation: Degree to which material palette aligns with target population's cultural associations. Misalignment (e.g., raw concrete in a Mediterranean domestic context) produces negative evaluation regardless of material quality.

context_congruence.interpretation: Material must match building typology expectations: marble in a bank = congruent; marble in a playground = incongruent. Context-material mismatch produces negative evaluation.
